title: Is the first number in each pair divisible by the second?
description: Four pairs of numbers are split into rows of primes. The row of the divisor is looked for inside the row of the first number in each pair.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is divisible by another when the row of primes of the other sits inside its own row, with every prime counted as many times. Watch for students who match primes without counting how often.

video_script.why: The child decides divisibility for four pairs by looking for the row of primes of the divisor inside the row of the number, counting each prime, the way the book does for forty two and twelve.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four pairs: two hundred and twenty five and twenty seven, ninety six and twenty four, three hundred and forty three and seventeen, nine hundred and ninety nine and ninety nine
video_script.anchor: four pairs of numbers, each with two rows of primes, and the row of the divisor ringed inside the row of the number or left hanging
video_script.payoff_line: Only ninety six is divisible by twenty four

final_answer.value: a. No; b. Yes; c. No; d. No

hold_back: a. No; b. Yes; c. No; d. No
maths_rules: 225 = 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 3 × 3: 27 needs three 3s, 225 has two, so 225 is not divisible by 27
96 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 and 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3: the row of 24 sits inside the row of 96, leaving 2 × 2 = 4, so 96 = 24 × 4
343 = 7 × 7 × 7 and 17 is a prime not in the row: 343 is not divisible by 17
999 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 37 and 99 = 3 × 3 × 11: 11 is missing from 999, so 999 is not divisible by 99
video_script.design: Each pair gets two rows of primes. The row of the divisor is ringed inside the row of the number, or a missing prime is left hanging outside.
